<entry id="P00393">
<head-word>עָזַב</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) [
<italic>to cut off</italic>,] </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to relieve an animal broken down under its load</italic> (v. 
<xref rid="Q01569">פָּרַק</xref>), 
<italic>help to unload</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Mekh. Mishp. s. 20 (ref. to Ex. XXIII, 5) פעמים שאתה חדל ופעמים שאתה עוֹזֵב at times you may abstain, at times you must help. Ib. פריקה מנין ת"ל עָזוֹב וכ' whence do we derive the duty of unloading? It says (Ex. l. c.), thou must release with him; B. Mets. 32
<sup>a</sup>. Tanḥ. Mishp. 1 עֲזוֹב קימעה מכאן וכ' loosen (the load) here a little, raise there &c.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to leave, abandon</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sot. 12
<sup>a</sup>; Ex. R. s. 1 (ref. to עזובה, I Chr. II, 18) עזובה … שהכל עֲזָבוּהָ Azubah is Miriam … for all (young men) left her alone (ignored her on account of her sickliness). Midr. Till. to Ps. X וציון אמרה עֶזָבַנִי וכ' and Zion said, he has forsaken and forgotten me. Ib. to Ps. XCII מי שמורה … ועוֹזֵב וכ' he who confesses his sins and forsakes (them, Prov. XXVIII, 1</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הֶעֶזִיב</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to untie, release; to effect a divorce</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. 32
<sup>b</sup> גט זה … לא יַעֲזִיב this letter shall have no effect, shall not untie, shall not release, contrad. to אינו מַעֲזִיב does not release, v. יָעַל.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>עִיזֵּב</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to make worth abandoning, make abominable</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yalk. Hos. 527 (ref. to Is. I, 4) אל תיקרי עזבו אלא עִיזְּבוּ read not, ‘they have forsaken’, but, ‘they have made (me) worth abandoning (caused me to be cruel); Tanh B’huck. 2 
<pgbrk id="pg1061" />עוזבו אתי (read עיזבו אותי). Pesik. R. s. 31 (ref. to עזבני, Is. XLIX, 14) עִיזְּבַנִי he has made me contemptible.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נֶעֱזָב</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be forsaken</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Lev. R. s. 35 (ref. to Ps. XXXVII, 25) נ' מיראתו וכ' forsaken of his fear of the Lord.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְעַזֵּב</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be abandoned, neglected, hated</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 45 ומִתְעַזֶּבֶת, v. כָּעַר; Cant. R. to II, 14 ומתעבת, ed. Wil. מתעובת (corr. acc., or read: מְתוֹעֶבֶת, v. תָּעַב). Pesik. R. l. c. והיו … ומִתְעַזְּבוֹת בפניהם and they became abominable and hateful in their sight.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="P00402">
<head-word>עַזּוּת</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (v. 
<xref rid="P00216">עַז</xref>) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> with פנים or מצח, 
<italic>insolence, effrontery</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kidd. 70
<sup>b</sup> כל כהן שיש לו ע' פ' וכ' (not בו) any priest that is insolent is surely one of them (the slaves of Pashḥur). Ib. אם ראית כהן בע' מ' וכ' if thou seest an insolent priest, do not criticise him, for it is said (Hos. IV, 4) &c. Sabb. 30
<sup>b</sup>; Ber. 16
<sup>b</sup> שתצילנו מעזי פנים ומע' פ' save us from contact with insolent men and from being insolent; (Rashi: from giving reason for the imputation of spurious descent, a sign of which is insolence). Taan. 7
<sup>b</sup> כל אדם שיש לו ע' פ' (Ms. M. עזות only), v. supra. Kidd. 49
<sup>b</sup> עשרה קבים ע' וכ' ten measures of insolence have come down into the world, nine of them Meshan took &c.; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>harshness</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Deut. R. s. 2 ענה אותו ע' gave him a harsh answer.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<italic>to be bright, intense</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sifra Thazr., Neg., Par. 2, ch. II, v. כָּהָה.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> ה' פנים 
<italic>to set one’s face against; to dare, be insolent</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Bath. 131
<sup>a</sup> והֵעַזְתִּי פני, v. יַלְדּוּת. Ber. 62
<sup>a</sup> עד כאן הֵעַזְתָּ פניך ברבך hast thou dared so much against thy teacher (as to enter into his private rooms)? Zeb. 102
<sup>a</sup> הָעֵיז פניך בו 
<italic>defy him</italic></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to strengthen, encourage</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Midr. Till. to Ps. CXVIII, 7 תָּעֵיזּוּ לבבכם (or תָּעִיזוּ, fr. עוּז) strengthen your hearts, take courage.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְעַזֵּז</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to become strong; to be daring, defiant</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Midr. Till. to IX, 20 (ref. to יָעֹז, ib.) אל יִתְעַזְּזוּן במלכותן ואל יתעזזון בשלותן let them not be defiant on account of their royal power, or on account of their prosperity; (ed. Bub., Chald. לא יתע' במלכותיהן ובלישניהון let them not be daring with their power or their tongues); Yalk. Ps. 645.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="P00408">
<head-word>עֲזִיבָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (עָזַב) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>abandoning, giving up, renouncing</italic> (in favor of the poor, Lev. XIX, 10).</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. 131
<sup>b</sup> וכולן … מ"ט ע' כתיב בהו and from all of them the owner must not derive the benefit of putting a person under obligation (v. טוֹבָה), because ‘abandoning’ (עזב) is written about them (Lev. l. c.). Y. Peah IV, end, 19
<sup>a</sup> שהן בע' they must be abandoned. Ib. V, beg. 19
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to תעזב אתם, Lev. l. c.) יש לך ע' אחרת כזו (it intimates that) there is another abandonment like this (renouncing one’s property in favor of the poor, v. הֶפְקֵר). Y. Ned. XI, 42
<sup>c</sup> bot. מעשר עני ניתן בזכייה ואלו בע' the tithe of the poor is given to the poor by way of a transfer (to a certain person), but these (gifts) are abandoned (the owner having no right of disposal).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>forsaking</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Lam. R. to V, 20 ארבעה דברים … מאיסה וגעילה ע' ושכיחה Jeremiah used four expressions: rejection, loathing, forsaking, and forgetting. Gen. R. s. 69 (ref. to Gen. XXVIII, 15) אין ע' אלא פרנסה forsaking refers to sustenance (with ref. to Ps. XXXVII, 25); Lev. R. s. 35; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>shunning, unworthiness</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ned. 22
<sup>a</sup> (in Chald. dict.) מלין דע' things which must be shunned (indecencies); (Ar. מלין דעֲזוּבָה things worthy of an abandoned woman).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup> כדי לעַטֵּר שוקי וכ' in order to have the markets of Jerusalem decorated with fruits; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְעוּטָּר; f. מְעוּטֶּרֶת;

XVII, 6) הצדיקים מִתְעַטְּרִין בבני בניהם ובניהם מתעטרין באבותם the righteous are saved for the sake of their grandchildren, and their children for the sake of their fathers; אברהם נתע בזכות וכ' Abraham was saved (from the furnace) for the sake of Jacob &c. Ib. יצחק נתע' וכ' Isaac was protected through Abraham, and Abraham through Isaac. Gen. R. s. 47, beg. (ref. to Prov. XII, 4, as applied to Sarah) בעלה נתע' בה והיא לא נִתְעַטְּרָה בבעלה her husband was protected through her, but she was not protected through him; a. e.</notes></sense>

<sup>a</sup> דסלקין לע' ודנחתין לתתא (for) those who go up (to Palestine) and those who come down (to Babylonia). Y. ib. VI, end, 15
<sup>c</sup> חדא מלע' וכ' one (grave) above and one below. Sabb. 30
<sup>a</sup> שאול … לע' מר' תנחום they asked this question over (the head of) R. Tanḥum, i.e. those standing by him when he was teaching (v. אֲמוֹרָא). Ḥull. 51
<sup>a</sup> לע' מרבי רבה with the great Rabbi when he was teaching; a. fr.—עִילוֹי 
<italic>upon him</italic>. Targ. Y. Gen. XXVIII, 13; a. e.—Y. Ber. II, 4
<sup>c</sup> bot. כד הויין תפילוי ע' when he had his T’fillin on. Ib. ולא סמכין ע' but we do not rely upon him, a. e.—[Usu. עִילַוֵּיה, v. עִילָוֵי, or עֲלוֹי, v. עַל ch.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>
